Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Junior Billing & Reconciliation Analyst role at Bask Health. You describe a job built around reconciling invoiced amounts against approved commercial agreements, investigating duplicate, missing or incorrect charges, and keeping clean reconciliation spreadsheets. The posting asks for zero to two years in a billing, finance operations or accounting role. I have nearly three years of billing and reconciliation work and would like to bring it to a software company.

As Financial Manager at AMG Family Dental in Belmont, I oversee pricing analysis, billing, collections and revenue tracking for a practice serving more than 1,000 patients each year. The core of the job is matching what was billed to what was actually paid. Improving our reporting and reconciliation in Dentrix led me to identify and recover over $500K in annual revenue, and I reduced A/R aging by 10% by streamlining claim submission and follow-up. I also wrote a Python script that automated the weekly insurance payment reconciliation, cutting it from five hours to one and flagging underpaid claims so they were followed up rather than forgotten.

At Northrop Grumman I audited more than 100 financial models for accuracy and controls and tracked program costs in SAP and Deltek Cobra, so documenting how a number was reached is second nature to me. My Excel skills are advanced, and I also use SQL and Python for larger data checks.

Your posting mentions comparing rates, discounts, credits and effective dates, escalating unusual issues, and working Eastern Time hours. I am in Massachusetts, so the schedule is natural for me. I am a U.S. citizen, available immediately, and glad to start in a junior role where the goal is accuracy first and speed second.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Alexander Airapetian
